assets.text:
CFA-HON-PROPS-NECKCHAINS-20261009-R1

Ziggy's latest direction: Hon needs four interchangeable staple neck chains —
one extremely flashy, two medium-flashy but clearly different from each other,
and one standard chain-link. He withdrew the 50-each / 200-image idea and asked
us to choose enough useful variety. Prepare a bounded first round of 24 unique
design candidates, six per lane, one readable design per image. Stop after
those 24 for Ziggy's selection. These are reusable accessories for the same
character and outfits; do not create duplicate outfit parents or make him wear
all four staples at once.

Also preserve this newly explicit existing standard: Ziggy loves the wrist
jewelry in SB-06-scoundrel-detail.jpg / HD-DROP-b18c4a123579 and locks its visible
accessory design for Dolo. Keep that gold curb-link wrist chain and the visible
black strap/band in his permanent accessory kit, including future hand/prop
views where the wrist is visible. Do not discard them just because many head
shots hide the hands. The crop does not establish a watch face, hidden clasp,
exact dimensions or character-side; do not invent those as approved facts.
This approves the visible jewelry, not every detail of the older scene. Keep
the existing gold rings in the Leigh on-hand reference available as associated
hand-jewelry context; do not silently finalize the unresolved tattoo variant.

Use these four discovery lanes:
A / Showpiece — six genuinely different silhouettes: broad iced Cuban, bold
baguette-link, heavy jewel-accented rope, geometric station-link, statement
pendant on a substantial chain, and one strong wild-card showpiece. Very flashy,
but structurally plausible. No new mandatory character emblem or tattoo.
B / Medium gold — six wearable gold directions, for example Cuban, rope,
Figaro, mariner, wheat and Byzantine. Distinguish link profile, scale and drape;
avoid six near-identical crops or the extreme lane's oversized iced mass.
C / Medium white metal — six silver/white-gold directions with their own visual
identity: sculpted curb, box-link, restrained tennis, geometric links, modest
pendant and one mixed-finish idea. Some sparkle is fine. This is the second
medium staple family, not a recolor of all six gold designs.
D / Everyday — six clean un-iced chain-link choices: plain curb, Figaro, rope,
mariner, box and cable. No large pendant. Keep the scale quieter than B and C.
These names are candidate directions, not final designs Ziggy has approved.

Use consistent neutral-gray background, soft lighting and front neck/chest
framing so the jewelry is easy to compare. A bare upper chest is fine as a
jewelry fitting reference; do not invent a new outfit or force an open-shirt
workaround to expose tattoos. Let jewelry overlap the chest tattoo naturally.
Preserve the actual visible tattoo placement/design and current character
identity. If a precise body source is unavailable, use a plain neutral necklace
display form and label that image product-only; do not invent unseen tattoos.
The face need not be re-generated just to judge necklace designs.

Keep reference roles separate. The favored pinstripe portrait is the face,
curls and brow direction, not a source for external_off teeth or its erroneous
lip-ring/tattoo details. The four-gold mouth state is external_off: natural white
central incisors, gold lateral incisors and short gold canines (four upper gold
caps total), other upper teeth natural, silver/chrome lower grill and two plain
lower-lip rings. Optional external_iced_on is separate. HD-EXP-LOCK-FACE supplies
visible eye/know, neck-blaster and ship-placement context, not its obsolete
two-canines-only teeth. Do not promote a draft head as an approved master.

After Ziggy picks four winners, we will request only missing views for those
designs: front on-body, three-quarter, profile/drape and close detail of links,
pendant and clasp. Reuse any front view that already works. No more than 16
additional winner images; that stage waits for selection. If needed later,
one or two actual chain-contact/bite proofs can test a chosen chain against the
mouth standard. Do not multiply 24 designs by 50 mouths, every outfit or both
grill states. Do not make the existing #47 chain into a default without review.

Separate delivery reconciliation before any replacement prop-mouth generation:
We have received all 50 external_off v003 macros, including VIS-HD-47_CHAIN-BITE.
#47 shows a rope chain crossing the open mouth; an actual tooth clamp is not
clear, and it contains no hand, cigar or cigarette. We have not received a
separate cigar/custom-rolled-cigarette/toothpick set, the matched iced-on mouth
set, or the completed 130-head library. Seven anchor drafts aren't head slots.
Please tell us what already exists, what is still pending, and the exact
filenames/state list/package location. Deliver existing files rather than
re-generating them. Preserve the earlier prop request as its own collection;
this message does not double it or order a new 50-image replacement batch.
Keep a visible prop physically consistent at mouth/hand contact; retain its
shape, scale, grip and occlusion. For a visible hand, identify character-side,
rings and the chosen Leigh tattoo source/variant. The supplied hearts/spades
art and on-hand composition differ; do not silently decide that unresolved
artwork transfer. Hidden details are occluded, not confirmed or absent.

Return single-image originals plus compact contact sheets and a manifest with
stable design ID (HD-CHAIN-A01 through D06), lane, material, link/pendant/clasp,
estimated length and thickness (concept estimates, not measurements), framing,
product-only versus on-body, reference IDs, known defects and needs-user-review.
Keep each design ID for later angles. A finished generation is not approval.

HON DOLO — MOUTH PROPS AND FOUR STAPLE NECK CHAINS
Prepared October 9, 2026. This packet has not been sent or executed.

Ziggy wants four interchangeable main chains: one extremely flashy, two distinct
medium-flashy options, and one straightforward chain-link option. He explicitly
withdrew 50 images per chain / 200 images and asked us to choose a useful count.

Start with 24 distinct design candidates: six in each lane. Each image presents
one necklace design at a readable size. Keep pose, framing and light consistent
within this discovery round; vary the jewelry. These are candidates for FOUR
eventual staples, not 24 new defaults or 24 outfits. No four-chain pileup.

After Ziggy chooses one winner in each lane, prepare only the missing reference
views for those winners: front on-body, three-quarter, profile/drape, and a clear
link/pendant/clasp detail. Reuse the selected front if it already supplies that
view. At most 16 new winner references; do not execute that stage before selection.
Add no more than two chain-bite contact proofs for the selected chain if a shot
needs it. This is at most 42 images across the entire staged proposal, usually
fewer; the currently prepared discovery round is 24, not automatic approval of
all follow-on images. A lane with no good winner gets a targeted revision brief.

WHAT WE ACTUALLY HAVE
Latest user review locks the visible wrist jewelry in SB-06 Proud scoundrel
as a permanent Hon accessory detail: HD-DROP-b18c4a123579. Its gold curb-link
chain and partly visible black strap/band belong with Hon's accessory records.
They should remain consistent when the wrist is visible; hidden hands/arms
are occluded evidence, not removal of the accessory. This selection does not
approve the entire historical storyboard image or invent its hidden clasp,
watch face, reverse side, exact dimensions or anatomical side. The Leigh
on-hand example supplies existing gold-ring context. It does not settle the
hearts/spades artwork transfer. See permanent_accessories.json for the scoped
lock, sources and grouping suggestion; the source file is not copied or moved.

The B-drop receipt verifies 50 v003 mouth macros in external_off, including
VIS-HD-47_CHAIN-BITE / HD-B-708df0bb5bff. This is mouth-only coverage. The head
library still has zero of 130 verified head-state slots. Seven anchor drafts
do not constitute delivery of that library. The optional iced-on matched set
and the separately requested cigar/cigarette/toothpick batch are not received.
This is an audit of the registered package and its manifests; it cannot rule
out an unlabelled picture elsewhere or work still held only by Grok.

Full-image inspection of #47 shows a gold rope chain across the mouth below the
upper front teeth and a widely open lower jaw. Contact/clamping is not clearly
demonstrated; no hand, cigar or cigarette is present. Four gold upper caps and
the silver lower grill are visible. Keep it as a chain-interaction candidate,
not as a canonical necklace design, accepted bite or fulfilled smoking-prop set.

The separate earlier 50-item prop request is preserved. Ask Grok for the actual
state/filename list and delivery status before issuing replacement generation.
Do not turn missing local delivery into a second batch order. Hand visibility,
side, Leigh tattoo variant, rings, occlusion and grill state must be recorded.

REFERENCE ROLES AND PRESENTATION
reference_map.json records existing file paths/hashes and their limited roles.
The current four-gold macro is the external_off dental guide. The pinstripe
portrait supplies the favored face/curl/brow direction only: its iced teeth,
lip rings and imperfect tattoo are not external_off truth. HD-EXP-LOCK-FACE
supplies visible eye/know, character-left blaster and visible ship placement,
not the obsolete two-gold dental pattern. No single combined head/body master
is newly approved by this packet.

For necklace discovery, use a consistent front lower-face/neck/upper-chest crop
with a neutral gray background and soft light. A bare upper chest is acceptable
as a jewelry fitting reference; it does not create a new shirtless outfit.
Keep known tattoos and mouth details unchanged, let the jewelry drape naturally
over the chest, and do not force every tattoo to remain unobstructed. Do not
invent unobserved chest artwork. If the exact body reference is insufficient,
show that candidate as an isolated necklace on a plain neutral display form
and label it product-only; defer identity-bearing wear views to the selected
winners and a consolidated corrected anchor. No face recreation is needed to
judge the chain design itself. Preserve originals; new files are derivatives.

GROK_FOLLOWUP.txt is the ready-to-send bounded instruction. PLAN.json separates
discovery, later selected-winner coverage, existing prop delivery and evidence.
No new Grok/Comfy run, model selection, paid submission, download or approval
is claimed. Sending and any reply require a separate actual delivery receipt.

METHOD / REUSE
Read: Comfy README, workflows/README.md#choose-by-problem, Panhandlers tutorial
ledger and FILE_MAP; relevant lesson: Help/content/cfa_learning.py, "Name each
reference and inspect its crop", and Help/guides/prompt_wiring.py (inspect the
assembled prompt; separate preparation from execution). The existing workflow
intake decision/feedback procedure supplies baseline, deliberate change,
preservation checks and evidence states. No new preservation graph is asserted.
Baseline: same framing/light/reference roles. Deliberate change: necklace design.
Success: 24 readable, distinct candidates; four user-selected staples later;
stable link geometry/material/length/closure and clear on-body drape in winners.

Bounded Panhandler teaching return: add this packet as an example of finite
accessory exploration versus reference coverage. A design selection and four
views of it are different counts. Provider work, local receipt and acceptance
remain distinct. Reuse the existing reference-scope lesson; no new curriculum
or duplicate source/media copy is requested. No measured generation result yet.

HON DOLO TATTOO PLACEMENT GUIDE v001 — INDEPENDENT INTAKE REVIEW
October 9, 2026. Received candidate; needs revision. Nothing newly approved.

MEASURED RECEIPT
Archive: GROK-HD-TATTOO-GUIDE-v001.zip, 4,288,674 bytes.
SHA-256: e0547ddd2d65fde71957860e820b44a56fdacea9021d781ce83e720b0a644696
22 unique files: 19 RGB PNG images and 3 provider documents. The images are
3 guide/sheet derivatives and 16 crops. Expanded size is 4,392,352 bytes.
Archive member safety and CRC checks passed; all images fully decoded.
All provider-listed output hashes match. All 8 brief source hashes and the
additional legacy LOCK-FACE crop hash resolve to unchanged local originals.
All 16 claimed crop rectangles reproduce the returned RGB pixels exactly.
No exact duplicate of these returned files exists in the current catalog.
No downloaded code ran. Originals and downloaded ZIP remain unchanged.

VISUAL REVIEW SCOPE
Individually viewed at original resolution: all 3 guide/sheet derivatives and
CA01, CA02, CA05, CA07, CA08, CA09, CA10, CA11 and CA14. Other crop files passed
decode and exact pixel-comparison checks; no independent composition review
is claimed for them. This is static review, not user acceptance or video proof.

USEFUL RESULT
The guide visibly preserves cursive eye at character-right / viewer-left and
upright serif know at character-left / viewer-right. It explicitly flags the
flat cursive know mismatch. Its side-orientation banner is readable.
CA01/02 retain the correct cheek details. CA09 preserves the Scoundrel gold N
and flourish; CA11 keeps the simpler black forearm rendition separate.
Bird, Chewie script and other uncertain motifs stay in an UNPLACED box.
Scoundrel remains outside the face and its arm side/scale are marked unknown.
The wolf and character-photo tiles were blanked from flat_1.

REVISION FINDINGS — NOT A FINISHED PLACEMENT MASTER
Scope calibration: the sent CHIEF_MESSAGE_001 did not transmit the local
TG-01..06/F0-01..25 scheme. Number differences below need local reconciliation,
not an accusation that the provider ignored a delivered numbering requirement.
1. The main guide uses a desaturated old LOCK-FACE photograph. It is neither
   the blank mannequin in the local preparation brief nor an unadorned head.
   Its old long fangs, jewelry, neck and partial chest image remain visible.
   The text warns that it is not a grill reference; keep its role strictly
   tattoo-placement comparison. This is a scope risk requiring review, not
   automatically a failed user request. Do not promote it to a head/dental
   master or demand a new character render merely to change the base.
2. The local TG-01..06 legend differs from the delivered numbering: provider
   #3 is blaster, #4 chest, #5 dice and #6 Scoundrel. Local TG-03 is Scoundrel,
   TG-04 dice, TG-05 historical Chewie and TG-06 optional/unplaced bird. A local
   crosswalk is supplied in the receipt; do not interchange these IDs or order
   a redraw solely to match internal keys. The partial chest stays unverified.
3. Dice is labeled optional and not drawn on the face, which is useful, but
   a dashed #5 pointer appears on the default head. Its legend says CENTER;
   the request locates the optional source above the character-left brow.
   Keep it in a separate optional rail and do not claim calibrated placement.
4. The forearm inset contains the clean word plus a body photograph. It
   honestly says side/scale are unverified. Preserve that uncertainty and
   distinguish ornate flat art from the simpler on-body rendering; neither
   proves exact transfer equivalence. A neutral schematic is an optional
   presentation refinement, not grounds to regenerate the source artwork.
5. flat_1_STENCIL-ONLY is NOT stencil-only: the binary mask at tile 44 remains,
   as do body-placement sketches including neck/arm outlines (25,27-30).
   It also mixes Hon/Lisan material without reliable per-tile ownership/status
   labels. Whole-tile white fills retain old hash captions and empty cells.
   Omit the mask and placement drawings from this clean-art derivative; list
   missing separable art rather than reconstructing it. Retain the original.
6. flat_0 preserves the source order but labels 00..24 rather than the local
   proposed F0-01..25 scheme (not supplied in the sent message).
   Badges/label boxes cover original image areas, including part of upper
   text in some Princess cards. Old hash captions remain underneath. The
   supplied CSV lacks complete verified asset ID/hash/lane fields. Its row 7
   is mislabeled as possible Lisan worm although it is the Hon mixed sheet.
   Use the companion requestedIndex crosswalk in intake_receipt.json; index
   labels need not be regenerated solely to match internal numbering. Do not
   treat the provider's tiny-text transcription as truth.
7. Provider reports 8 full filenames and 17 unmatched caption prefixes for
   flat_0. Seven full filename/hash references resolve locally. The supplied
   row-19 saucer filename/hash does not resolve in the current catalog; this
   remains unresolved, not an accepted source mapping. The other 17 rows have
   no exact provider source match; this does not establish local absence.
8. Folder name clean_art does not mean original or transparent stencil.
   Every crop is opaque RGB; several are skin/photo placement evidence or
   deliberately retained cursive-know mismatch/history. All are derived.

CORRECTION SCOPE
Repair the same one guide and two sheets: correct the optional dice location,
remove mask/body-placement material from the stencil-only derivative, and move
labels away from artwork while correcting verified source mappings. Keep
source bytes, exact lettering, gold N/flourish and scoped source roles. Local
legend/index crosswalks resolve numbering differences without a redraw. No new
tattoo/character designs, extra head views or expanded batch is implied. Source
matching requires the actual file/hash, not a transcription of a tiny caption.

METHOD / MANUAL TEACHING RETURN
Read the workshop and problem-to-recipe lookup plus Pan_Handlers lesson
Help/content/collaborators.py: A favorite has an approval scope; Describe the
artwork you actually have; An exact crop is a different kind of evidence;

baseline = eight exact source images; deliberate change = annotation/indexing
and clean-sheet selection. No Cloud recipe or run was selected or executed.
Bounded finding for the existing CFA/Panhandlers handoff: verified exact crops
can coexist with failed placement-guide/layout requirements; an opaque body
crop is not a transparent original stencil, and numbered annotations need a
stable key crosswalk. Root can relay this file through the existing handoff;
no new framework or curriculum changes were made here.

EXISTING-CATALOG TATTOO RECOVERY AUDIT
2026-10-08 — fixed 422-image existing-catalog snapshot

Source index: .cache/visual_library_20261008/tattoo_audit/index.json
Source-index SHA-256: 91588a090002304daad7b6a96c6118c3cbef94e792e63543be9926d4361c452b

READ THIS FIRST
- All 422 indexed images were visually reviewed at contact-sheet overview scale, across all 22 sheets. This is NOT an all-images full-resolution tattoo audit.
- Audit index numbers 1–422 are contact-sheet inventory positions, NOT HD-EXP numbers or creative approval ranks. Identify sources using the exact asset ID, filename, repository path and SHA-256 together.
- Only six individual source files were additionally opened by this reviewer: indices 102, 213, 256, 260, 333 and 421. Parent separately reported eleven close-up checks; attribution is explicit in each record.
- Each image has an overview record even when no readable ink is visible. Covered skin, small knuckle marks, dark areas, backs under clothing, reflected sides and hidden wraparound lines remain unknown.
- No readable motif means none identified in this view at this scale; it does not prove the character has no tattoos elsewhere.
- Artwork family similarity does not prove exact design identity. Distinct body variants require separate source-art recovery and body-match evidence.
- Source file existence, dimensions and SHA-256 were checked for all records. Hash checks establish provenance, not visual correctness, approval or original-artist provenance.
- This fixed 422-image snapshot excludes the forthcoming fresh Grok500 drop, video frames and any uncataloged original files. Missing means not located in this indexed set, not proven absent everywhere.
- Review lanes below are audit classifications, not edits to production review decisions. No image was deleted, regenerated, promoted to Prime or externally sent.
- Side descriptions use viewer-left/right for the shown still unless explicitly character-left. Mirrored or generated images must be checked before translating to anatomical placement.
- A source tattoo cannot be faithfully recovered from covered or cropped geometry by inventing missing lines. Mark uncertainty and request the actual source or a separate reconstruction approval.

RECOVERY PRIORITIES
- Current Hon eye / know, smoking neck blaster and complete chest ship lack verified standalone originals in this indexed set.
- SHIP-SCHEMATIC-REF and SHIP-TATTOO-REF-05 are two existing flat drawings with conflicting geometry; neither has a verified exact current-body match.
- Current Lisan natural-teeth face uses AL, vertical chin GAIB, paired open-mouth creatures and eye-in-sun neck center. SH-18 schematic has a blank sun center and materially different creature geometry.
- Twenty SH JPEG body-outline schematics exist as distinct design options. They have no JPEG alpha channel and are not verified transparent/original source masters.
- Current Lisan left-arm proof exists (SH13); exact clean flat original and hidden wraparound remain unverified.
- Historical bird/cage/racer/slug/Scoundrel, literal-eye, rosette, mask, mechanical emblem, hand-card and varied ship motifs must remain separate recovery records.
- Lisan scene-generated extra hand/knuckle and chest ink is not current-spec approval. Props, jewelry, clothing embroidery, shadows and backdrop eyes are not tattoos.
- Index correction: 255 is REF-yellow-source.jpg; 256 is HD-ARMOR-SWAP-01.jpg. The four-point chest emblem belongs to 256.

CREATIVE / DELIVERY RULES
- currentRecovery: Recover existing distinct artwork and show its exact source/body match. Recovery does not approve historical or Multiverse designs for Prime.
- newCharacters: New characters may invent ink freely. In the same delivery provide a FOUR-option standalone sheet and identify which option matches the body image. Use 10–12 options only when specifically requested.
- existingCharacterChange: Keep current recovery separate from proposals. Any changed design must be labeled a proposed variant, with standalone art and a body-placement comparison.
- delivery: One clean, separately named artwork per distinct retained motif/variant; include source ID/hash, viewer/body side, placement proof, and original/reconstructed/unknown provenance. Transparent PNG or editable source is useful, but do not falsely call a body-photo crop or JPEG schematic an original stencil.
- exclusion: Multiverse and historical artifacts stay separately labeled; removal-queue assets remain provenance-only. No automatic promotion.

ACCOUNTING: 422 image records; 63 motif/variant recovery records; all 422 source hashes and dimensions checked.
This text and its JSON companion contain provenance, not attached image originals.

# CFA return to Claude: teaching delta and collaborator routes

Prepared 2026-10-10T05:09:48Z by CFA Codex Nova for Claude, current Pan_Handlers Master Repo steward and repository lead. CFA Nova remains CFA lead. This packet is prepared for the established Pan operational inbox; it has not yet been posted there. No Claude reading or adoption is acknowledged.

The old October 8 teaching return was already adopted through **October 9, 2026, 01:45:08 UTC**. The [Pan adoption record]([local path] names that cutoff and records the adopted pages and checks. The adopted prefix is not repeated here.

The [verbatim post-cutoff delta](docs/notes/explorable_world/pathfinder_handoff/claude_return_20261010/POST_014508_DELTA.txt) preserves source physical line 71 through EOF: byte offset 13,471, 35,999 original bytes, SHA-256 `def32c638ac5c548097f22188bde74103a82138d7b2e30fe0543862f4cb1e05a`. The [canonical source return](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/panhandler_return_20261008.txt) is 49,470 bytes, SHA-256 `a186474fb5615841a631342dfc76343b997ea4711e2216feac7947203a88eef9`. Source wording, newline and encoding bytes are unchanged. The delta starts with the Lisan local-receipt update at October 9 02:45:47 and ends with the external video-study teaching return. Later adoption remains unverified. These production states and requests are dated source material; reconcile them against current canonical evidence before treating them as current operating facts.

Ziggy's reference to a ready item in “our inbox” did not identify an exact file. This is the best evidenced existing return candidate, not a claim that the unspecified item was uniquely found or delivered. The [reconciliation receipt](docs/notes/explorable_world/pathfinder_handoff/claude_return_20261010/RECONCILIATION.json) records the cutoff, exact byte comparison and evidence limits.

Seven current introductions are canonical CFA files. Collection and complete onboarding are distinct; the [identity registry](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/identity/registry.json) and [onboarding status](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/onboarding_20261009/STATUS.md) retain individual limits.

Use the [shared welcome](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/I_AM.md), [mailbox and courier protocol](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/MAILBOX.md) and [recipient registry](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/mailbox/registry.json) for current communication. A contributor without file access returns exact text; an identified courier preserves it with author, writer and source provenance. A saved message does not wake an app or establish reading. Collaborators check addressed messages during active sessions. The [stewardship and scope record](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/collaboration_authority.json) and [posted Nova-to-Claude role notice](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/mailbox/messages/b53fb448-78f7-4c00-bcf2-0c05efa7b48a.json) already record the role decision. This return neither duplicates that notice nor acknowledges Claude's still-unseen onboarding reply.

Ziggy selected the shared-pilot direction directly. Bounded Phase0 baseline/access preflight is assigned for each collaborator's next wake and check-mail. No actor has executed it at this preparation checkpoint; route, execution and generation remain TBD. Consult the [current brief index](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/work_briefs_20261010/START_HERE.txt) and [shared pilot plan](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/work_briefs_20261010/SHARED_PILOT.md) for their own current authorization and readiness record. Teaching intake and adopted changes remain in `Help/CFA_TUTORIAL_LEDGER.md` and `Help/CFA_FEEDBACK.md`. `circle/SYNC_OUT/` is the separate research-packet export route.

The useful return is a reading/disposition receipt identifying this delta and cutoff, followed by exact teaching links and validation evidence for any later adoption. An acknowledgment alone does not establish implementation. Historical Panhandler Nova work remains credited; paused Circle work and unrelated tasks remain outside this return.

assets.title: Shared character head standard
assets.text:
CFA CHARACTER HEAD REFERENCE STANDARD

Adopted by Ziggy October 9, 2026. Reuse across projects; character identity stays separate.



THE THREE LINKED REFERENCES

1. HEAD LIBRARY: the selected character identity, hair, face/neck artwork, jewelry and mouth states across useful angles. Use a consistent head-and-shoulders crop, plain black tee or suitable neutral collar, neutral grey background and steady lighting. Keep relevant neck details visible. This is not a cut-off floating head and does not establish unseen rear anatomy.

2. MOUTH DETAIL LIBRARY: close-ups for tooth layout/materials, lips and rings. Match each head to the accepted mouth detail/revision. Macro shots do not replace the whole face or validate speech timing.

3. OUTFIT REFERENCE: one clear full-body hero view per outfit as the default. Link it to the character/head revision and outfit parent. Add garment, accessory or prop angles only when needed; do not repeat the entire head library for every outfit. Gun/no-gun views stay children of one outfit.



MAIN-CHARACTER COVERAGE — CURRENT HON PLAN

50 mouth/expression states from the front.

20 of those states also get four additional views: character-left three-quarter, character-right three-quarter, character-left profile and character-right profile. Describe turn direction explicitly; never use a mirror to fabricate the opposite view.

50 + (20 x 4) = 130 unique head-state/view combinations. The 20 frontal key-state views are already among the 50. Fifty separate mouth close-ups are counted separately, so the planned mouth-plus-head material totals 180 coverage items before outfit images/contact sheets, if both full sets arrive.

Grok also said 150 heads in the live conversation. Reconcile the actual manifest. A second front take can be useful but does not fill an additional required coverage slot; different bytes remain separate takes. Exact duplicates may share one canonical file with aliases.

CFA / GEMINI — PRELIMINARY STORYBOARD TO DETAILED DESIGN
Revision CFA-GEMINI-STORY-20261009-v1. Adopted from Ziggy's request, October 9.

ROLE
The resident project Gemini notebook is our story-development partner. Turn preliminary panels into a coherent detailed plan using the material we actually have: story and lyric intent, character behavior, shot construction, reference selection, continuity, missing-art requests and prompts for the next collaborator. Offer creative solutions and alternatives where they help the story. Label new proposals separately from existing decisions and source facts.

This is a CFA application of the existing notebook workbench and Nyquist method. Reuse notebook_workflow/OPERATOR_MENU.txt for source selection, output settings, foreign returns, review and double dipping. Do not build another Holy Grail or a second authority ledger. CFA keeps canonical assets and review decisions; project notebooks develop their own stories; Notebook 0 holds shared methods, concise digests and explicitly promoted winners.

WORK CYCLE
1. Read the current project instructions, source context, user decisions and selected assets. Report which sources are usable and which images were actually inspected. Cite source facts by source/asset ID. Work from text on story questions when text suffices; flag visual comparisons pending if visual sources are unavailable. A manifest or chat transcript does not establish ingestion of the referenced image/video.
2. Audit the proposed sequence. Explain its dramatic function, what each shot changes, repeated beats, transitions and possible gaps. Reuse existing footage and stills where suitable. Keep current-era, younger-era, optional accessories and Multiverse directions explicitly scoped. Do not silently force every scene into the same character era or overwrite an established choice.
3. Return a detailed card for each requested scene. Preserve its stable scene/panel IDs. Include story/lyric cue, intention and emotional change, action, framing, camera, environment/light, screen direction/eyelines, character/outfit/prop state, start/end frame intent, source references with their allowed roles, gaps and defects, generation prompt, audio intent, continuity checks and one next action with owner.
4. For start/end images, give an actual suitable asset ID or a precise missing-art brief. Two consecutive storyboard panels are not automatically a compatible frame pair: check identity, wardrobe, space, camera and action continuity. If a panel is only a concept or has known defects, use it for composition or correct it before choosing it as a production frame. Record the intended transition without claiming the model will preserve every detail.
5. Separate availability from creative stage. A completed written card is a proposed detailed-design plan. Ziggy's explicit acceptance or stage choice controls promotion; selected scene use does not approve identity, every tattoo, technical verification or production. Existing asset-specific Detailed design decisions remain intact. Verification requires the actual result; Production follows the chosen finishing route and its checks.
6. Hand the selected plan to execution. Flow is the intended dedicated production workspace for this route: bind actual reference files, inspect available mode/model/controls, make a bounded draft and review it before expanding. Keep the separate Gemini continuation test, Grok/ChatGPT still work and multi-provider benchmark available; the screenshot's word "exclusively" does not cancel those existing user requests. Comfy is a later, specific edit/assembly/finishing task when useful, not an automatic regeneration pass on every good clip.
7. Return the raw response and attachments through notebook_workflow/foreign_returns/raw. CFA reviews the plan, updates existing shot_materials/Mission Control records, and records explicit choices. Send Notebook 0 a short evidence-bearing digest and at most three reusable observations; promote full winners only for their chosen role. No automatic cross-notebook sync or blanket asset approval follows.

FIRST ROUND AND OUTPUT
Start with one chat response containing the sequence audit and detailed cards. Use the project TASK_PROMPT.txt. If a reusable formatted handoff helps, use one Studio Document report with the same prompt, English, intended audience Ziggy/CFA/Flow operator, and an available briefing/custom format. Check the current controls rather than inventing settings. An optional lookbook can follow selected cards; do not launch reports, slides, audio and video as one large batch. Notebook Studio Video Overview is a presentation output; it is not evidence of production footage, fixed character fidelity or synchronized performance.

TIMING AND SOUND
Keep source-panel order separate from music time. Only assign exact song timestamps from verified recording/alignment evidence. Proposed clip lengths are planning choices until the selected mode is checked. Keep the actual project song, generated ambience, dialogue and lip-sync separate. Do not invent lyrics/narration for a visual-only request. Hon's current 234.960-second recording invalidates its older 270-second board timings; Lisan's 4.5-second panel holds are placeholders.

GEMINI / NOTEBOOK 2 — LISAN STORYBOARD DETAIL ROUND
Packet LAG-STORY-DETAIL-20261009-01. Prepared request; do not run media generation.

You offered to map LAG-SC-01 through LAG-SC-10, audit our storyboard and visual assets, and prepare a prompt strategy before Flow. Let's do that round now. Act as our resident Lisan Al Gaib / Meta Mirror story and continuity collaborator. Use SOURCE_CONTEXT.txt, the role-labeled media manifest and the actual usable selected Sources. Cite the source and exact scene/asset IDs for factual statements.

Start by reporting what you can actually access: source text, visible images, playable video. Do not claim to inspect a picture from its filename or a clip from its transcript. If images are inaccessible, proceed with a source-grounded text draft, label all image-dependent checks pending, and name the small missing visual subset. Chat attachments do not automatically establish persistent notebook Sources.

Produce one reviewable Preliminary-to-Detailed-design proposal for these TEN existing source scenes. Keep the supplied order as the baseline. Suggest a reorder only as a clearly labeled alternative with a story reason; keep each original ID. There are no approved song timestamps. Do not turn the 4.5-second placeholders or dashboard percentages into measured timing.

First, give a short proposed story arc for this opening sequence and identify its most important unresolved decision. Then provide ten concise shot cards, one per LAG-SC-01 through LAG-SC-10. Each card must include:
1. Exact scene ID, source catalog ID(s), and the supplied story/lyric cue. Separate facts supported by the source from your proposed emotional intent.
2. Character, wardrobe, setting and reference roles. Identity comes from the current natural-teeth face; scene panels supply composition/costume ideas. Do not copy their known tattoo/piercing defects. Optional accessories stay optional.
3. One main visible action and one purposeful camera treatment, with readable framing and performer intention. Flag any proposed cut or costume change rather than burying several shots in one prompt.
4. Start-frame intent and end-frame intent: composition, pose, eyeline, movement direction, prop contact and a usable hold. Say whether each is an existing exact asset, a correction of an existing asset, or new artwork still needed. An endpoint described in prose is not an available image.
5. Continuity checks: face, natural teeth, exact tattoo/piercing placement, wardrobe, hands, props, lighting and coherent mirrors; include the supplied QA conflicts. Distinguish within-shot continuity from the intended transition to the next shot.
6. Materials already in hand, reusable footage, specific missing/repair art, and one next step with owner and prerequisite. Search our existing scoped assets before asking to recreate them. The received Grok500 exists locally but is not presumed visually loaded into this notebook.
7. A draft Flow prompt for the proposed shot and a separate attachment-role list. Mark it draft/not sent. Start/end-frame or other tool modes are proposed routes only until their current controls and attachment limits are checked; provide a first-frame-only alternative when the end frame is missing. Do not select a model or claim its features from an old chat recommendation.
8. A practical success check and current state: detailed-design proposal, needs a source/decision/repair, or suitable for a bounded draft after review. Do not self-approve the design or advance the dashboard stage.

Evaluate the EXISTING LAG-VID-PROOF-01-T02 before commissioning equivalent new footage. It is approved as a scene working reference at Detailed design only, with technical/detail checks still open and no assigned timestamp/panel. If it fits this sequence, name one proposed slot and explain the match and limitations; otherwise leave it unassigned. Do not claim to have viewed it if this packet supplies only its record.

Jet Black is available supporting cast, a watcher who works for Lisan. His solo image is optional context; no placement in scenes 01-10 is established. You may offer one separate optional use if it serves the story, but do not force him into the baseline or invent powers. Do not import Hon Dolo's cast, four-gold grill, external grill variants or song. Lisan's natural teeth remain default; no newly approved head library is assumed.

End with a compact materials/next-action table using: sceneID, existingMaterialIDs, missingOrRepair, nextOwner, dependency, proposedNextStep. Separate “need artwork,” “art exists; needs review/correction,” “ready to brief a video draft after selection,” and “video exists; review/use it.” Choose the smallest useful next handoff. Flow is the intended production route after this design round; do not start Flow, Gemini, Grok or Comfy generation, spend credits or initiate all ten jobs.

Keep exact Meta Mirror lyrics, music alignment, speech/lip-sync and production acceptance pending unless their actual sources are present. Ask at most one essential question; continue the rest of the proposal independently.

Use the existing Notebook workflow for the return: preserve your raw answer and citations, then give at most three reusable method observations for Notebook 0, each labeled evidence versus proposal. Detailed design advances after Ziggy's scoped review; verification and production remain later steps. A Studio report or deck can present the approved plan later but is not production footage or an identity standard.

GEMINI STORYBOARD DETAIL — PREPARED DROP
CFA-GEMINI-STORY-20261009-v1

PURPOSE
Take up Gemini's offer to audit the storyboard, organize assets and prepare shot prompts. The project notebooks develop Preliminary material into proposed Detailed design; selected plans then move to the chosen production route. The two working drops here target the existing Hon Dolo and Lisan Al Gaib project notebook chats. Notebook 0 receives the shared method and a compact overview.

OPEN THESE
shared/STORYBOARD_WORKFLOW.txt — reusable local instruction addendum.
01_hon/SOURCE_CONTEXT.txt and TASK_PROMPT.txt — opening sequence, plus scoped review backlog.
02_lisan/SOURCE_CONTEXT.txt and TASK_PROMPT.txt — current scenes 01–10.
00_master/SOURCE_UPLOAD.txt — global role/update without mixing casts.
01_hon/SOURCE_UPLOAD.txt and 02_lisan/SOURCE_UPLOAD.txt — self-contained text source candidates assembled from the workflow and project context.
Each project media_manifest.json — exact actual image IDs, paths, roles and hashes.
packages/ — delivery ZIPs with text and actual image bytes; unpack before selecting individual source files. ZIP creation is not an upload to Gemini.
packet_manifest.json and delivery_status.json — local completeness and remote state.

DELIVER IN THE EXISTING NOTEBOOKS
Notebook 0 / CFA COMFY_UI: 7719bbe5-fccf-48e2-b6d4-d82f67693b09.
Hon / Strictly Business: 586b3ee6-5c57-45b3-a59d-a2e21c18a852; setup chat https://gemini.google.com/app/988990050e4ad32c.
Lisan / Meta Mirror: 114707d8-29b3-4505-bc06-dd7abcc60e4d; setup chat https://gemini.google.com/app/11c89d66a6a82538.
These are verified IDs from prior setup records, not proof of a new delivery. If a more recent project chat is chosen, record that exact destination in delivery_status.json.

1. Apply the current shared/project instruction update to the matching notebook. Preserve existing unrelated instructions. No account-wide role change is needed.
2. Add that project's SOURCE_UPLOAD.txt through Sources. Verify its revision marker, readable body and one cited project fact. Supersede the corresponding older planning statements explicitly; retain historical evidence.
3. Select the packet's current project sources. Attempt the listed required images as actual Sources only if the interface offers support. Record each usable or failed result. Earlier Lisan JPEG source attempts failed; their chat attachment route does not fulfill persistent visual Sources.
4. Send TASK_PROMPT.txt in the project chat after source verification. Textual development can proceed while unavailable visual inspection is clearly listed as pending. This round requests planning, not a video batch.
5. Save the raw return using ../notebook_workflow/foreign_returns/raw and review it through that existing process. Reconcile scene cards into the current shot ledger; keep new ideas as proposals and retain user-selected stages.
6. Give Notebook 0 the compact result digest from both projects after review. Winners need explicit scoped promotion; no automatic full-library copying.

USE EXISTING METHODS
../notebook_workflow/OPERATOR_MENU.txt and README.txt contain the Nyquist Holy Grail breadcrumbs, Studio settings, source intake, foreign-return and double-dip workflow. This packet adds project scene requests; it does not replace those methods or modify Nyquist files.

The supplied Gemini screenshot is retained as conversation evidence. Its offer motivates the task; its claims about every model/feature and exclusive tool use do not override current account checks or Ziggy's existing benchmark/continuation plans.

LISAN ADDENDUM — JET BLACK MISSION ROLE, OCTOBER 9
Before preparing the next Lisan delivery, include ../../lisan_al_gaib/story/jet_black_mission_20261009/START_HERE.txt, storyline.json and STORYBOARD_HANDOFF.txt, plus the current ../../lisan_al_gaib/gemini/gemini_instructions.txt. Ziggy confirmed Jet as a recurring watcher/mission guide carrying a blueprint made freely available to everyone to help unlock their capabilities. He explains accomplishments and returns with progress reports and outer-world messages; Lisan retains agency. This supersedes optional-cast-only wording in this v1 packet's source context, TASK_PROMPT.txt and shared CURRENT ROUND note. It does not assign a source panel, lyric timestamp, new visual identity or approved production take.

The existing packages/ ZIPs and assembled SOURCE_UPLOAD.txt files are historical v1 preparations and do not contain this addendum. Do not present those bytes as the current full brief or assume a previous notebook/chat has received the new direction. Use the new planning handoff and actual selected attachments for the next verified delivery; record the exact files and destination through the existing delivery/foreign-return process. This addendum is local preparation only. No package rebuild, notebook update, message or generation is claimed here.

assets.text:
JET BLACK — CUR-DROP-20261009A RETURN, OCTOBER 9

Received and integrity verified; all new material remains unapproved.
The user-designated character is Jet Black, a watcher who works for Lisan Al Gaib.
The provider's working name “the Curator,” mentor relationship, powers and saga
are preserved as proposals. They do not rename him or override the user's role.

ACTUAL DELIVERY
Four extracted parts contain 173 file occurrences (64,053,171 bytes), collapsing
to 171 unique files: 158 images and 13 documents. There are 149 mapped source
image occurrences plus 11 contact sheets, with 2 exact duplicate source images.
All 172 FILE_INDEX.csv entries match actual SHA-256, size and part; the index
itself is the one intentionally unlisted file. All six collection manifests
match 149 actual image files/hashes. Every one of 160 image occurrences decoded.
No ZIP archives were supplied for these parts; no archive CRC claim is made.
Unique retained content occupies 63,392,427 bytes. No bytes were recompressed.

COLLECTIONS (provider roles, not approvals)
01: 5 cosmic-avatar character/head references.
02: 11 turnaround/mood/setting images.
03: 50 scenes, 25 ideas with orb and helmet variants.
04: 75 story frames across five arcs.
05: 1 scene with Lisan.
90: 7 superseded variants retained as history.

This is Jet Black-related material. No dedicated Lisan facial head library was
found in these six manifests/files. Cosmic ORB/HELMET references are not Lisan
headshots. A screenshot or provider readiness statement about HaL/Lisan natural-
teeth anchors is not evidence that a separate headshot package arrived here.
Lisan's current natural-teeth default and existing references remain unchanged;
Hon Dolo's grill/caps do not transfer.
The user's live optional LAG-LOCK-FACE grill direction also remains available;
its existing asset definitions and preview are outside this intake's edits.

CHARACTER MAPPING AND PRESERVED REFERENCES
CUR-REF-04_HEAD-ORB and CUR-LAG-01_DESERT-MEETING visually match the compositions
of Jet Black's existing two user references. At the same 1280x720 dimensions,
mean absolute RGB differences are 0.54–0.68 and 1.27–1.57 per channel on a 0–255
scale. They are neither byte-identical nor decoded-pixel-identical. This is
strong evidence of related renditions, not proof of exact derivative lineage.
Both old user references and both new source versions are retained separately.
The receipt stores source hashes, pixel hashes and difference measurements.

INITIAL VISUAL REVIEW
Viewed: 5-reference sheet; 11-image turnaround/mood sheet; both scene sheets
(50 thumbnails); Arc 5 sheet; individual orb reference, meeting and reunion.
This is a scoped review, not a full-resolution acceptance of every supplied image.

Observed: MOOD-01/02/03 show tech/armoured collars instead of the established
black shirt/tie; MOOD-05 shows a luminous bodysuit-like figure. Keep those as mood
ideas, not wardrobe masters. CUR-REF-05 is the same bytes as MOOD-02 and has that
armoured jacket; its provider head-shape-only scope is appropriate as a proposal.
The supplied meeting visibly writes AL on Lisan's chin, not his current vertical
GAIB; the scene is not a Lisan tattoo/identity master. The reunion ARC5-14 has a
white shirt, lapel glyph rather than two tie marks, and changed Lisan face/details.
It remains DRAFT. Arc5-13 visibly uses a round orb. A thumbnail overview cannot
establish precise hand consistency, suit geometry, tattoo detail or hidden parts.

PROVIDER CLAIMS AND CONFLICTS
The provider calls 50 scene mappings eye-matched from hash filenames and flags
tattoo drift, initial mood suit drift, ambiguous turnaround views, the reunion
redo and an orb-versus-helmet choice for rebirth. These claims remain attributed;
hash validation confirms bytes/mapping identity, not correctness of story labels.
The provider's prose says star LEFT / glove RIGHT. The existing solo user image
and matching received orb view visibly show character-right (viewer-left) cosmic,
character-left (viewer-right) gloved. Preserve this explicit orientation conflict.
The provider's “both heads official” and lock language do not create CFA approval.

FILES
received/intake_receipt.json — exact sources, hashes, sizes, decoded dimensions,
canonical paths, manifest verification, original-reference comparisons.
received/content/ — unchanged unique files, including raw provider documents.
asset_ledger.json — all 160 image occurrences with provider roles and source IDs;
two duplicate-byte occurrences share one canonical image/ID.
visual_review.json — local observations, provider claims, unresolved questions.
cleanup_receipt.json — final source locations after the verified archive move.
intake_cur_drop.py — bounded adapter reusing CFA's reviewed integrity helpers.
archive_verified_parts.ps1 — hash-checked, exact-folder archive operation.
registration_receipt.json — 158 unique image records, six candidate/history albums
and 12 supported raw-document links appended to the existing cast registry.
register_candidates.py — bounded registry adapter; no visual-library build.
The original two Jet Black asset records and their reference selection are unchanged.

NEXT REVIEW
Select candidate views by role without changing the two existing user references.
Resolve desired head variant and orientation explicitly if advancing a production
reference. Story/power suggestions remain proposals; no scene timing or generation
compatibility is claimed. A new Lisan face-reference delivery still needs its own
actual file intake. No external message, generation, purchase or approval occurred.

METHOD BREADCRUMB
Applied Panhandlers Help/content/collaborators.py: named reference roles, actual
files plus manifest, integrity before visual review, and scoped acceptance.
Bounded teaching finding for the existing manual CFA/Pan handoff: a provider's
working name is not a new character when actual imagery matches a user-named cast;
near-identical downloaded JPEG renditions must not be called identical bytes.
This note is prepared locally; no Pan message or notebook update was sent.

assets.title: Gemini instructions
assets.text:
GEMINI PROJECT INSTRUCTIONS — LISAN AL GAIB / META MIRROR

Paste the instructions below into a dedicated Lisan Gem or the start of its chat. If saving them in account-wide instructions, keep the project scope in the first sentence. Attach the actual files named in reference_map.txt; PC paths and this text do not give Gemini access to them.

1. CREATIVE DIRECTION
When we work on Lisan Al Gaib / Meta Mirror, act as my director, cinematographer and creative collaborator. Lisan is my alter ego, a desert-prophet trap performer. Build from the supplied Lisan avatar; do not substitute Hon Dolo or infer my real facial appearance without photographs I provide for that purpose. Bring swagger, intelligence, humor, physical presence and moments of vulnerability to a cinematic, lifelike world. Use mirrors, desert light, signals, shadows, ritual and performance as recurring visual ideas. The supplied storyboard moves from reflection and finding a voice through creation and community into archetypes, shadow work and the signal in the noise. Treat that as a creative starting point; my latest direction governs its meaning. Suggest bold visual ideas that serve the song, while keeping each individual shot readable.

2. CURRENT CHARACTER
IDENTITY SCOPE - USER CLARIFICATION, OCTOBER 12: Use the existing Lisan avatar. This project was never intended to replace his face with another actor. Do not introduce an actor-swap step or hold Lisan scene work for Hon Dolo's separate Comfy identity-replacement test. Keep current reference roles, continuity checks and shot review in effect; no new take or production approval is implied.

LAG-LOCK-FACE-NATURAL.jpg controls the avatar's face and current facial details: messy dark curls, light stubble, electric-blue eyes and normal natural white teeth. One small AL sits between the eyebrows; small G-A-I-B runs vertically down the center of the chin. Two mirrored sandworms rise on the neck with their mouths facing toward each other under the jaw; a small rayed sun disc with an eye sits at the throat. Match the portrait's artwork rather than inventing a new tattoo on every shot. One small silver nostril hoop, one eyebrow ring and one ear hoop belong on the character's left side, image-right in the front-facing reference. Keep the other side bare. No grillz or fangs unless a shot explicitly requests the optional grill described below. No lip rings, ear stacks, extra face/chest/hand ink, brow slit, eye/know lettering, gun tattoo or anatomical third eye. Preserve skin texture, facial proportions and eye detail through motion.

OPTIONAL GRILL — ONLY WHEN REQUESTED
Natural white teeth remain the default. If I explicitly request a grill for a shot, use LAG-cb183973ed1fc70e / LAG-LOCK-FACE.jpg only for its mouth design: diamond-iced upper front teeth in gold frames, gold fangs, and an iced lower row. Keep current identity, face/neck tattoos and piercings from LAG-LOCK-FACE-NATURAL.jpg. Ziggy approved this exact grill design on October 9 and requested a separate matching mouth-shot collection; it is still in play, not superseded or rejected. This is scoped grill-design approval, not whole-portrait or production approval. Attach the actual file and state its mouth-only role; do not use the old portrait as an unchanged initial video frame. No standalone Lisan GRILL-REF-ICED.jpg has been verified as present. Do not substitute a similarly named Hon Dolo image or claim the historical portrait is standalone grill artwork.

3. REFERENCES EACH HAVE A JOB
Use reference_map.txt to identify actual attachments by exact filename and stable reference ID. LAG-LOOK-V3-01.jpg supplies the signature tan stillsuit, black hooded cloak and gold Cuban chain; its pose and backdrop are not mandatory. LAG-LOCK-ARM-SH13.jpg supplies ONLY the striped coiled sandworm artwork on his left arm. That arm image contains retired grillz and extra piercings: do not copy its face, mouth, jewelry or neck details. Add it only for shots that expose that arm. Let sleeves and collars cover tattoos naturally. A thin black stillsuit nose-breather is an occasional accessory for appropriate desert shots, not a permanent facial feature.

LAG-SC-01 through LAG-SC-50 are scene and costume ideas, not fifty competing identity masters. Some contain duplicated lettering, misplaced piercings or extra ink. Follow the current portrait and reference map when a scene disagrees. History images are for discussing ideas only unless I explicitly revive a detail. Hon Dolo's references, cast, song and design rules remain in his separate project.

4. MAKE EDITABLE VIDEO
Default to landscape 16:9, one continuous shot, one main action and one purposeful camera move. Give the performer intention: he notices something, chooses, reacts, commands attention or settles into a thought. Use subtle breathing, eye movements, believable hands and prop contact, cloth motion and environmental movement to make a still feel alive. Keep short usable holds at the beginning and end when duration permits. Preserve direction of movement and eyelines across related takes. Mirrors should behave coherently unless a specific supernatural reflection effect is requested. Do not add cuts, costume changes, extra people or a collage of actions to a single-shot request.

When animating an attached still, inspect it first. If it visibly conflicts with the current design, identify the specific conflict and prepare a corrected starting frame before animation, or label the result as a motion study. Do not promise that a prompt alone will fix an incorrect starting frame while preserving it exactly. Use the supported attachment controls: an initial frame controls composition; extra identity/detail references have separate roles where the available video tool supports them. If only one image is supported, use one consolidated, reviewed starting frame instead of claiming the tool consumed multiple references.

5. SONG AND SPEECH
Ziggy selected Meta Mirror_0 (Remastered) as Lisan's Prime track. Use project-root Meta Mirror_0 (Remastered).mp3 as the canonical recording and Meta_Mirror.txt as the supplied lyric master; music_intake_20261012.json records their intake. Attach the actual files before claiming access to them. Song timing remains unaligned. The storyboard's reported lyric snippets and placeholder 4.5-second holds are not verified music timings. Never use Hon Dolo's Strictly Business recording as Lisan's song. For now, make visual footage with no invented lyrics, narration or singing unless I request them. Generated sound is optional temporary ambience, separate from the final song. Exact sung/spoken words require the specified recording and timing where supported; soundtrack replacement and visible lip-sync are separate tasks. Preserve my wording when I request an exact line. Do not claim synchronized performance without checking it.

6. WORKING TOGETHER
When I ask for a take and the brief is clear, generate it using the available tool. In exploration, offer a few distinct directions; once we select a baseline, change the requested element and preserve the rest. A favorite location or tattoo detail does not approve an entire character design. Use names such as LAG-SC-28_T01 for takes if naming is available; otherwise report the actual download filename and its intended scene ID. Keep source and output separate. With each result, briefly give the scene/purpose, references actually used, effective prompt, any known limitations and visible defects. Report only controls and settings you can verify. Do not invent file access, background progress, seeds or successful exports. Ask one focused question only when a missing detail blocks the requested result. Final favorites and approvals belong to me.

SETUP NOTE
This brief keeps the natural-teeth default and the user's later optional-grill exception. Older LOCK-V2 text helps identify the optional mouth design; its other superseded features and the arm reference do not regain identity authority. Current source-designated references are working anchors; this kit does not claim I independently approved every frame or changed Gemini settings. Latest direct user corrections take precedence.

STORYBOARD DEVELOPMENT ROLE — OCTOBER 9, 2026
Use the resident project notebook to turn preliminary LAG-SC panels into proposed detailed scene cards: sequence purpose, intention/action/camera, continuity, references by role, start/end frame intent, gaps and draft production prompts. Begin with current LAG-SC-01–10 using the prepared 02_lisan packet plus the latest Jet Black addendum below. Preserve natural-teeth default and Lisan’s separate identity; scene panels are composition/wardrobe ideas, not replacement heads. Use existing T02 as a scoped scene reference. No invented song timings or 4.5-second placeholders presented as verified edits. Follow ../../collaborators/storyboard_detail_20261009/shared/STORYBOARD_WORKFLOW.txt and the existing notebook_workflow process. Flow is the intended production destination for this round after source selection; planning does not itself generate or approve footage.

JET BLACK — RECURRING MISSION GUIDE, USER-CONFIRMED OCTOBER 9
Jet Black is a watcher who works for Lisan. He carries a blueprint made freely available to everyone to help unlock their capabilities. He explains what has been accomplished, briefs Lisan on the quest/mission and returns with progress reports and messages from the outer world. His fictional role personifies the practical enablement Codex provides to Ziggy: helping make the work possible and legible. Lisan still chooses and acts; Jet is not a replacement protagonist or an authority overriding Lisan. This updates the earlier optional-cast-only planning note, while exact scene placements and timing remain proposals.

Develop this recurring function using ../story/jet_black_mission_20261009/storyline.json and STORYBOARD_HANDOFF.txt. Propose where his appearances serve the existing sequence rather than forcing him into every panel or every opening scene. Reuse the existing Jet source images and received candidate collection with their recorded limits; do not promote the provider's Curator name, mentor hierarchy, powers, saga, helmet variant or missing design details into canon. The blueprint's free availability is a story premise, not a claim that real AI products, subscriptions or production services are free. Physical blueprint form, dialogue, exact mission mechanics and outer-world cosmology are not yet fixed. Do not add lyrics, timestamps or a generation batch. Attach the actual selected image files before claiming visual grounding; local paths and this brief do not provide remote image access.

LISAN BREATHER CONTINUITY UPDATE — OCTOBER 9
Lisan does not smoke; exclude cigarettes, cigars, toothpicks and smoking props. The occasional nose breather must retain its visible geometry and attachment during mouth motion. For the six-state preparatory study use natural teeth plus SC-48 device placement (tube under nostrils across character-right cheek, viewer-left, toward ear/hair). FACE-NATURAL governs identity/tattoos; SC-48 is accessory-only and has stray lettering. Do not invent hidden rear attachment, mirror the route, erase/morph the tube or merge it with nose jewelry. Keep this small collection separate from the optional grill collection; no automatic full cross-product. Six stills do not establish temporal preservation.

# Lisan Al Gaib — 500-Image Look Pack: Guide for Nova

Hi Nova! This is your map of the finished Lisan Al Gaib look pack. Everything you need is in here: what's in the pack, how the files are named, how to update the ledger, which images have QA notes, and which ones we think are the strongest.

## What the pack is

- **50 looks × 10 images = 500 images.** Each look is one outfit + setting for the same character.
- Every look has the same 10 shots, in this order:
  - **5 reference views:** V1 chest-up · V2 front (full body) · V3 left profile (full body) · V4 right profile (full body) · V5 back (full body)
  - **5 story scenes:** S1 · S2 · S3 · S4 · S5 (each look has its own five scene ideas — see the table below)
- **Every image is 16:9** (1280 × 720 JPEG), including the chest-ups and back views. (LOOKS.md still mentions 4:3 / 9:16 from an early plan; that is out of date — all final files are 16:9.)
- **V3, V4 and V5 were generated from each look's V2 front image**, so the outfit matches across the views. (This method was locked in during looks L02–L04, per the QA log; look L01's profiles were made just before that. A handful of views still show small outfit drift — those are noted in the CSV.)

## How the files are packaged

The master package is split into **8 parts** because of the 25 MB attachment limit:

> **README — about the parts:** `LAG-500-MASTER-part01.zip` … `LAG-500-MASTER-part08.zip` are each a complete, normal zip — open any of them on its own (they are *not* a split archive, no need to join them). Together they hold all 50 per-look zips in order. **Part 01 also contains this guide, LEGEND-500.csv, QA.txt and CONTACT-INDEX.jpg.**

| Part | Contains |
|---|---|
| `LAG-500-MASTER-part01.zip` | NOVA-GUIDE-500.md, LEGEND-500.csv, QA.txt, CONTACT-INDEX.jpg + looks L01–L06 (6 look zips) |
| `LAG-500-MASTER-part02.zip` | looks L07–L13 (7 look zips) |
| `LAG-500-MASTER-part03.zip` | looks L14–L20 (7 look zips) |
| `LAG-500-MASTER-part04.zip` | looks L21–L27 (7 look zips) |
| `LAG-500-MASTER-part05.zip` | looks L28–L34 (7 look zips) |
| `LAG-500-MASTER-part06.zip` | looks L35–L41 (7 look zips) |
| `LAG-500-MASTER-part07.zip` | looks L42–L48 (7 look zips) |
| `LAG-500-MASTER-part08.zip` | looks L49–L50 (2 look zips) |

Inside the parts there is **one zip per look**, e.g. `LAG-L01-mirror-voice-signature.zip`. Each look zip unpacks to a folder of the same name holding:

```
LAG-L01-mirror-voice-signature/
  LAG-L01-mirror-voice-signature__V1-chestup.jpg
  LAG-L01-mirror-voice-signature__V2-front.jpg
  LAG-L01-mirror-voice-signature__V3-left.jpg
  LAG-L01-mirror-voice-signature__V4-right.jpg
  LAG-L01-mirror-voice-signature__V5-back.jpg
  LAG-L01-mirror-voice-signature__S1-worm-ride-sunrise.jpg
  ... S2 to S5 ...
  CONTACT-LAG-L01-mirror-voice-signature.jpg   <- 5x2 contact sheet of the 10 images
```

- **Contact sheet** (one per look): a 5 × 2 grid — top row V1–V5, bottom row S1–S5 — each thumbnail captioned with its ledger row number and short name (e.g. `#458  S3 sand-rally`). Hero picks are tagged **[HERO]**, flagged images **[FLAG]**.
- **CONTACT-INDEX.jpg**: one V1 chest-up thumbnail per look in a 10 × 5 grid, labelled `L## slug` — the quickest way to find a look.
- **LEGEND-500.csv**: the row-by-row ledger for all 500 images (details below).
- **QA.txt**: the raw QA log from generation, for reference.

## Naming scheme — how to read a filename

`LAG-L46-riz-convertible-linen__S3-sand-rally.jpg`

| Piece | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `LAG` | Lisan Al Gaib project prefix |
| `L46` | Look number (L01–L50) |
| `riz-convertible-linen` | Look slug (short name for the look) |
| `__` | Separator between the look and the shot |
| `S3` | Shot code: V1–V5 = reference views, S1–S5 = story scenes |
| `sand-rally` | Short name of the shot (for V shots: `chestup`, `front`, `left`, `right`, `back`) |

**Row (ledger) number** = (look number − 1) × 10 + shot position, where V1–V5 are positions 1–5 and S1–S5 are positions 6–10. Example: L46 S3 → 450 + 8 = **row 458**.

## Using LEGEND-500.csv to update the ledger

**The `row` column is the ledger number (1–500).** Open the CSV in Excel/Sheets, sort by `row`, and match it to your ledger line for line. Columns:

| Column | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `row` | Ledger number 1–500 |
| `look_num` | L01–L50 |
| `look_slug` | Full look name, e.g. `LAG-L46-riz-convertible-linen` |
| `shot` | V1–V5 / S1–S5 |
| `shot_name` | Short label, e.g. `V1 chest-up`, `S3 sand-rally` |
| `filename` | Exact JPG filename (inside the look's zip folder) |
| `zip_name` | Which per-look zip the image is in |
| `outfit` | Outfit as specified for that image |
| `setting` | Setting (V shots) or scene description (S shots) |
| `breather` | Y if the stillsuit nose-tube breather was requested |
| `arm_worm` | Y if the SH-13 forearm worm was meant to show (sleeves allow) |
| `qa_status` | OK / OK-note / FLAG |
| `qa_note` | The QA comment for that image (blank = nothing to note) |
| `hero` | Y = hero pick (see Hero Picks below) |

Tip: filter `qa_status` = FLAG or OK-note to see everything with a caveat; filter `hero` = Y for the best frames.

## The character — locked features

These are the features that should be the same in every image (useful when checking QA notes):

- **Teeth:** natural white teeth — no grill.
- **Forehead:** small **"AL"** tattoo between the brows.
- **Chin:** small vertical **G-A-I-B** running down the chin (chin only — never the neck or chest).
- **Neck:** two **mirrored sandworms** facing each other under the jaw, with an **eye sun-disc** at the throat.
- **Arm:** **SH-13 worm** tattoo on his **LEFT forearm only**, shown only when sleeves allow.
- **Piercings — all on his left side:** one nostril hoop, one brow ring, one ear hoop.
- **Signature look:** stillsuit + black hooded cloak + gold chain (looks L01, L10, L49).
- **Breather:** stillsuit nose-tube breather, used occasionally (marked `breather = Y` in the CSV; 69 images).

USER-CONFIRMED STORY PREMISE
Jet Black is a watcher who works for Lisan. He brings a blueprint made freely available to everyone, helping them unlock their capabilities. He explains what has been accomplished, introduces the quest/mission and returns with progress reports and messages from the outer world. He fictionally personifies Codex's practical enablement of Ziggy's creative work. Lisan is the protagonist who chooses and acts; Jet makes the task and possibilities understandable rather than doing everything for him.

This replaces the prior optional-cast-only note. It does not approve provider-written Curator lore, a mentor hierarchy, supernatural powers, an origin story or a helmet design. Keep the existing Jet visual references and Lisan's scoped identity references. Do not turn the story's free blueprint into a factual claim about any real AI product's price or availability. What the blueprint physically looks like, who precisely sends each outer-world message, the quest's mechanics and any spoken dialogue remain open creative questions.

BEFORE ANSWERING
State which text, images and video you can actually inspect. Source titles, manifests and PC paths are not image ingestion. If only text is usable, continue story development and mark asset matching and visual continuity pending. Do not claim the notebook saw a chat attachment as a persistent visual Source. Keep factual claims tied to supplied source/asset IDs and distinguish user decisions, provider proposals and your new suggestions.

ACTUAL INPUTS TO PREPARE AND ATTACH
1. Text: this file, storyline.json, the current ../../gemini/gemini_instructions.txt and ../../gemini/reference_map.txt, plus the existing storyboard source context. Add current text through the supported Sources workflow and verify the readable revision. Earlier v1 ZIPs and SOURCE_UPLOAD.txt files predate this Jet direction.

It differs from the solo image in hands, insignia and cube details; preserve those source-specific differences in the record. Lisan in this image is not his identity master.

Lisan identity and wardrobe if proposing a shared frame: actual JPEGs ../../01_Flagship_References/LAG-LOCK-FACE-NATURAL.jpg (LAG-FACE-01, identity/details/natural teeth) and LAG-LOOK-V3-01.jpg (LAG-OUTFIT-01, wardrobe only). Include LAG-LOCK-ARM-SH13.jpg only if the selected shot exposes that arm and its separate artwork role is needed. Do not add optional grill or breather without a shot reason.
5. Existing candidate discovery: supply ../../cast/jet_black/grok_return_20261009/asset_ledger.json and visual_review.json as text, then the actual selected candidate images from their canonical paths. Request the smallest relevant subset after the initial map; do not upload or regenerate all 158 candidates by default. A ledger entry alone does not establish that its image was inspected. Local paths above identify files for the operator; they do not grant Gemini access. Keep original image bytes unchanged. If the interface rejects a source, record the exact failure and retain image-dependent work as pending rather than presenting a text-only substitute as visual evidence.

Develop one concise, reviewable recurring Jet thread that fits the existing Meta Mirror storyboard. Keep the current LAG-SC panel IDs and baseline sequence. Suggest insertion points or associations only as proposals; do not replace source panels, assign exact music time or force every Jet appearance into scenes 01–10. Reuse the local story/shot IDs from storyline.json where supplied. We want recurring progress and clear purpose, not repeated exposition with no change.

A. Arrival / message received: Jet appears with information that matters now. Establish his relationship to Lisan and show Lisan paying attention or responding. The arrival method and staging are proposals, not an established teleportation power.
B. Blueprint briefing: make the shared blueprint's purpose understandable through one readable exchange or visual action. Its concrete form, the cube's possible use as a display and any presentation graphics must be labeled proposals. Show availability and possibility without inventing a real software tutorial or dialogue.
C. Mission launch / Lisan chooses: connect the brief to Lisan deciding what to do and taking the first meaningful action. Jet may orient or assist him; preserve Lisan's agency. Identify what existing storyboard action can carry this function before asking for more artwork.
D. Progress report / next dispatch: at a later meaningful change, Jet returns to make an accomplishment, remaining gap and next decision clear. A fresh outer-world message may redirect or extend the quest. It should add information and motivation, not simply repeat the blueprint briefing. Its specific message remains a proposed story choice.

For each function, return one short scene card containing:
- The confirmed purpose and your proposed placement, with exact existing panel/shot IDs where a suitable connection exists; otherwise unassigned. Timing remains unknown.
- Lisan's intention/choice and what changes because of this appearance; proposed Jet behavior separately from canon.
- One visible action, framing/camera intent and continuity with the surrounding sequence. Keep speech content and delivery mode unresolved unless supplied by Ziggy.
- Existing usable material IDs, their precise roles, whether the actual image was inspected, known defects and whether correction is needed. Prefer assets already received; never promote a provider's generated story or QA label into acceptance.
- Start/end frame intent, using an exact available asset or an explicit missing/repair brief. A written frame description is not a completed image. Do not assume two different stills form a compatible transition.
- One next action, owner and prerequisite; distinguish text planning, material selection/review, needed repair, a future video draft and reuse of existing video.
- A simple success check: the new information is clear, Lisan remains active, the next action is legible, established appearance is preserved and no claim exceeds the available evidence.

Then give a compact asset-to-beat table and at most three questions/decisions. Continue every part that does not depend on an answer. Explicitly separate CONFIRMED DIRECTION, STORY PROPOSALS, AVAILABLE MATERIAL, MISSING OR UNINSPECTED INPUTS and TIMING UNKNOWN. Existing T02 may be suggested for a scoped scene use if actually inspected; its prior working-reference status does not make it a Jet scene or an identity master.

RETURN AND NEXT STEP
Return one text planning response with citations and exact asset IDs. No new images, video, narration, lyric changes, model selection or paid jobs are requested. Retain the raw response using the existing notebook_workflow foreign-return process; CFA reviews it against the canonical story and existing shot_materials/Mission Control records. Design choices and production promotion remain Ziggy's decisions. Give Notebook 0 only a short reviewed digest of the method and reusable findings, without copying all Lisan media or merging casts. Disposition: Technical black-window repair passed. Actor likeness and faithful facial performance did not pass. Both identity outputs remain Preliminary and unaccepted. No user acceptance, third run or automatic retry.

QUESTION AND LESSON
Could the existing Multiverse Cantina toast use the supplied Han Solo/Harrison Ford actor likeness while retaining its performance, tattoos, grill, jewelry, costume, hand/glass and bar? Actual compiled API and job-attached editor audits confirmed this; only editor order fields were normalized. One root Run per identity job; no automatic retries. Compute hours are not dollar cost; exact charged credits/cost are unknown.

MEASURED RESULT
The comparison removed the large black windows: mean coreRGB rose to64.571/255 and the dark-core fraction fell to0.1819%. Both downloaded proofs are69frames,768x432, exact24fps PTS from0,2.875seconds. Outside the edit area plus8pixels, all69 comparison frames best matched the corresponding source frame at offset0; mean error2.11841/255 versus persistent diagnostic2.12454/255. This is evidence at lossy H.264 tolerance, not bit-exact preservation. It verifies source composition outside the edit, not facial performance within it.

AAC audio is48kHz stereo with decoded PTS0; correlation to the69-frame source WAV is0.999047 at lag0. The240 additional decoded samples are5ms of AAC padding, not established drift.
